utterances.text: Thank you. In the reports you looked at, was there any mention of the position of one or both stabilisers in relation to the explosion itself? And was that position usual in respect of the place where the explosion took place?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not in a position to tell you where the stabiliser was found. The stabiliser or these stabilisers. All I can say is that one stabiliser was found. It was analysed. The registration numbers were -- was recorded, and the specialists put that down on paper. I have no other information about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We have finished with Markale. Let's move on. Can we have page 23 of your statement in the French version; page 17 in English; and page 31 in the B/C/S. Here you speak of the protests. In connection with this part of your statement, a document is mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we call up 65 ter 11193.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This document is dated the 28th of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We should move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Lukic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you, Your Honour. Could we now please have ERN 01176 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're asking for an ERN number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's not, sorry. It's 65 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 65 ter, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a video, is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: There's a document on the list, pardon me. That's 10176. Perhaps that's what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's on the Prosecution's list.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, we have a document before us that deals with this event of the 28th of June. It was compiled on the 29th of June. It's the UNMO/UNPROFOR HQ that is sending it. In the first paragraph, below the heading, it says: "At the 28th of June, a UN Military Observer coming into the PTT building, parking his car on the lower parking place, observed the following: Heard and saw an outgoing projectile across the parking place and road, from grid," and then there's a numerical reference, "(the place is on BiH territory, approximately 1.800 metres from the nearest CFL)." My first question is the following. On that day, did only one such projectile explode, or were there more of them?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That day, on the 28th of June, 1995, there was, as far as I know, two shots of this type of homemade projectiles. One that hit the TV building, and the other one that fell on the street, in the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The third bullet point in this document says: "The projectile was following a low trajectory, travelling directly from firing point to target, and hit the TV building on the northern side, facing the British Cymbeline building." First of all, let me ask you the following: You have already been asked about this. Do you doubt the reports of the Military Observer who claims, in this report, that that projectile came from the territory that was under the control of the Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a report that -- that commits only the author thereof. That's what I said already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the Chamber would be greatly assisted if we would know where approximately grid BP 866587 would be, because that's what the witness says and that allows us to better assess what the witness could see and hear from the PTT building where he was parking his car. Could you assist or could the witness assist? I take it that the parties would not disagree on a -- yes, I see that the witness is raising his hand. Could you please assist us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Your Honour, it would be easy to check that the co-ordinates that were specified by the observer were those of the parking lot of the PTT building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the grid reference is to the place where he was at the time, as far as you are concerned? That's clear. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My next question, sir. In this paragraph, there is also a reference to another radar for monitoring mortar fire. In addition to the two French ones that you mentioned, there's a reference here to the British radar; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again, no, sir. If it were about the second French radar that was deployed in the Rajlovac sector, these Cymbeline radars, the first generation thereof for trajectories were built by the British, so this what brings about some confusion in your mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If anything brings me into confusion at all, it is this reference to a building here right next to the TV building. And it says here that this projectile hit the northern side of the TV building, facing the building where the British Cymbeline was. Which building faces the northern side of the TV building?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the text in English seems quite clear to me. The projectile hit the TV building on its north face, which is facing the building where the radar, British Cymbeline radar was set up. The Norwegian Captain Hansen probably mistook the British manufacturer of this item and the French user thereof.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now I'd like to dwell on this date, the 28th, a bit more. Is it correct that at that time a major Muslim offensive was launched and forces from Sarajevo were involved, as well as forces from Zenica, and forces from Tuzla? The objective was for the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina to get to the Drina. Were you aware of this operation, or were you only familiar with what was going on in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was aware of the whole of the operations that were launched by the Bosnian Muslim forces, since the 15th of May, in the region. I had general knowledge of the operations outside of Sarajevo which was not within our area of responsibility but which was for information only, and I was aware for action of the events that were taking place in Sarajevo, within that sector, and so I can confirm that with -- jointly with the actions that were led outside, the forces of the 1st Corps that were within Sarajevo attempted to break the lines of their adversaries in both sectors that were mentioned, one in the south, in the direction of Lukavica and Debelo Brdo, and the other one within the direction of Stup and Ilidza, to make it simple.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And that operation was part of this broader operation, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I could agree with you on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in relation to your statement, we need page 32, paragraph 2 in French; page 23, second paragraph of the English version; and page 43, fourth paragraph of the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When this is found, could I ask a few questions. Could you tell us, Witness, what is approximately the distance between the PTT building and the TV building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The -- the approximate distance is about 800 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you assist me in better understanding the report we had on our screens, where one UNMO reports that he saw an outgoing projectile across the parking place, and you said that was at the PTT building where he saw that; and further down it reads: "Another UNMO was on the parking place at the same time and he reported the following: He heard the sound of an approaching rocket motor. The round was fairly close and that he took cover." And then, on the next page: "He heard the impact but no detonation." And: "The UNMO stood up, and after a few seconds, there was a tremendous explosion at the base of the TV building." It -- it seems to be contradicting, the one saying I saw a projectile being fired from where I was, and the other one saying there was an incoming projectile, same time, same place, apparently. Then he hears the impact. I take it that if it doesn't explode, that it's not easy to hear an impact at a distance of 800 metres, and he, nevertheless, says that there was a tremendous explosion at the TV building after a couple of seconds. I'm totally lost as to how to understand this information, which seems to be partially presenting an outgoing round from the PTT building and a kind of a mixed report on an incoming projectile, which then later explodes at a great distance from there. That's my confusion. If you can help me out, please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will try and do so, Your Honour. There was, indeed -- there were two projectiles that were fired. One around 9.30 a.m. One hit directly one of the sides of the TV building, while the detonation was rather significant and the destruction also, I checked that myself afterwards, the other -- the other impact is the one that I was specifying, that did -- hit the road and made a crater there. And the author says that the explosion was not heard, which is surprising. The impact was true, real, and the crater is also concrete.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for this explanation. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for having taken us back to this document I've forgotten. You know that that I rarely seek admission into evidence but I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: May I just verify that this is document 10176?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think it is.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Then document 10176 receives number D134, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D134 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, we should go back to the statement again, P749. I've already said that in the French version, we need page 32, the second paragraph; in the English version, we need page 23, second paragraph from the bottom of the page; and, in the B/C/S version, page 43, fourth paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the paragraph above they ask you to look at a document. It's a protest dated the 8th of June, 1995, that General Gobillard sent to General Milosevic. You say, in your response: "This letter concerns events which took place in the southern part of the city in the sector of the Jewish cemetery and in Debelo Brdo between the 15th of May and 15th of June. Units of the Bosniak army 1st Corps attacked the crest line which overlooks Sarajevo in that sector. They moved closer to the UNPROFOR post in the sector located in Debelo Brdo. The Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, which was defending that position, retaliated with artillery fire and tanks and launched several well-targeted counter-attacks. The problem was that the SRK response was disproportionate to the attack and the SRK disregarded any possible collateral damage ..." Again, we are in this period of fierce fighting initiated by the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the 1st Corps, was, indeed, at the origin of these -- of this fighting, and I should remind you, a number of operations, pre-operations, for their adversaries.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could I ask one additional question. The last portion of what was read to you reads as following, and I'll do it in French: "[Interpretation] The SRK bombed the city and responded to the attacks by the Bosnian side. This is at least the way the SRK perceived the situation." What was preceding, that is, the description of the military operations, and the counter-attack? Was that an example of what you said in the last line, meaning that it also attacked the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This comment, when I read it again, is, in my mind, the example I provided for the lack of moral fiber and this disproportionate attack. The random shelling on the town was reported by the SRK correspondents who said that this was in retaliation to other attacks. General Gobillard and other people reminded our contact people that these actions could not be perceived as proportionate retaliatory acts. As regards what happened between 15th May and the 15th of June, I'm talking now from a professional standpoint, if the offensives launched by the 1st Corps of the Muslim forces could have been better organised, well, the reaction of their opponents of the SRK could have been more measured and would have had the same effect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: These attacks in your area of responsibility launched by the Muslim forces always came out of the part of the town that was considered to be a protected area; right?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my area of responsibility, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it also correct that the number of the members of the 1st Corps was disproportionately high compared to the membership of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was the number of the attacks by the BH army on the positions of the SRK disproportionately higher than the attack launched by the other side?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, certainly when these attacks were launched. However, you seem to omit the conditions under which the population and the units were living, subjected to constant random shellings, subjected to a blockade. Under these conditions, it is not surprising, is it, that this party felt aggressed and wanted to release the strangle-hold it was caught in?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You know what? There's one thing that I don't understand. I can't understand that an officer of the NATO pact would be speaking of disproportionate use of force when we know that Tomahawk rockets were used to target the inhabited or built areas of town without the opposite side having any possibility to return fire. Isn't that what you would call disproportionate use of force? If there's no possibility of response whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like you to tell me when between May and October 1995 Tomahawk missiles were used in the area of Sarajevo. I like to hear about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about the principle involved. Since you testify here as an officer of the NATO pact about the disproportionate use of force --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This witness testifies as a witness of the truth and not in a specific capacity. Your previous question was introduced by a desperate cry-out of not understanding something, is which comment rather than question. You may put questions to the witness, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No consultations in the courtroom. Write it down on a note and give Mr. Mladic, if he needs, a pen and a piece of paper. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When bombing the Serb positions in the surrounding area of Sarajevo, when NATO was bombing these positions, was there a disproportionate use of force at that time?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Listen, I can state that the force used was artillery fire, on the one hand, and air-strikes on the other. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: since from the beginning of July onwards when the first artillery pieces started arriving, the use of this force was always extremely measured, extremely cautious, and a great deal of attention was paid to do all we could to avoid casualties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you aware of the fact that Pale -- the Pale hospital was hit by the Mirage. Did that amount to a disproportionate use of force?

utterances.speaker: RM055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I know what the date of the incident, please, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There are two questions first, whether you're aware of the Pale hospital being hit. Are you aware of that? And if Mr. Lukic has a date, that might assist. Do you know of any such hit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am aware of fire hitting Pale, not the hospital in particular, but I believe the date is important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But it is about the hospital. If you do not know anything about the hospital being hit, then, of course, we can move on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I cannot confirm that the hospital was hit. I don't believe so. I'm wondering whether there isn't a confusion on a previous attack against Pale.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Notes. No consultations. Mr. Mladic. Well, the witness may have knowledge about Mirages firing at the Pale area, but seems not to be familiar with the hospital being hit, which makes the next question superfluous, it looks, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm also I'm looking at the clock at this moment. Yes, could you give us an indication as to how much time you would still need tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think one hour, one and a half hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One and a half hour. Ms. Hochhauser, could you give already an indication, as matters stand now, how much time you would need for re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I -- as matters stand now, Your Honour, I would estimate about half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: About half an hour. All the estimates for the witness -- the other witness to come this week, are still solid?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: From the Prosecution's point of view, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, any reason to believe that you'd need more than you asked for, for the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that my colleague Ivetic will fit it in the time he asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because we try to avoid any surprises at the end of this week. Then ... [Interpretation] I would like to ask you not to communicate in any way about your testimony with anyone. We expect to see you in this courtroom at 9.30 tomorrow. We shall finish your testimony tomorrow. Thank you. [In English] We turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I'm not going to wait until we see an empty public gallery. We adjourn for the day, and we will resume tomorrow, Wednesday, the 23rd of January, at 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 23rd of January, 2013, at 9.30 a.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
